title: Cache Telemetry Overhead Profiling Guide (KV/Prefix Cache v2)
author: Marcus Reed
body:
h1. Cache Telemetry Overhead Profiling Guide (KV/Prefix Cache v2)

h2. Purpose
This playbook describes how to measure and validate the performance overhead of the KV/prefix cache v2 telemetry instrumentation in the serving runtime.

We use it to answer:
* Does cache telemetry change p50/p95 latency, throughput, or GPU efficiency in a statistically meaningful way?
* Is overhead bounded across representative traffic mixes (sequence length distribution, cache hit-rate, streaming vs non-streaming)?
* Are new code paths safe for production rollout (feature-flagged) and do we have clear rollback triggers?

h2. Scope
This document covers:
* Runtime hot-path overhead (prefill and decode) due to:
** cache lookup/insert/evict event hooks
** request correlation / outcome classification (hit/miss/partial)
** saved_prefill_ms estimation and hit-bytes accounting
* CPU overhead (thread contention, allocations, logging/serialization)
* GPU overhead (kernel scheduling impact, stream syncs, extra memcopies)

Out of scope:
* Telemetry pipeline ingestion cost (handled by Platform/Telemetry)
* Dashboard query performance
* Customer application overhead

h2. Definitions
* *Baseline build*: runtime without v2 cache telemetry (or with instrumentation compiled in but fully disabled)
* *Telemetry-enabled build*: runtime with v2 cache telemetry enabled via feature flags
* *Overhead*: change in key metrics when comparing telemetry-enabled vs baseline under identical load
* *Hit-rate regime*: cache hit-rate bands used for testing (low/medium/high)

h2. Ownership and expected cadence
* Primary owner: Marcus Reed (Perf validation & runtime perf tests)
* Runtime instrumentation lead: Omar El-Sayed
* Sign-off required from: Logan Wright (Telemetry spec), Sean Gallagher (SRE)

Run this playbook:
* Before enabling v2 cache telemetry in any production region
* For each major runtime train that modifies cache hooks or telemetry payload format
* When we change sampling defaults, hashing/bucketing, or request attribution logic

h2. Acceptance thresholds (go/no-go)
All thresholds assume identical model, hardware, and load shape.

h3. Primary (release gating)
* *Latency p95 (end-to-end)*: +<= 1.0% increase (or +<= 3 ms, whichever is larger)
* *Latency p50 (end-to-end)*: +<= 1.0%
* *Throughput (tokens/s per GPU)*: -<= 1.0%
* *GPU utilization*: no sustained drop > 2 percentage points (averaged over test window)
* *CPU (runtime process)*: +<= 3.0% CPU time per request at fixed QPS, or +<= 1 core per 8 GPUs equivalent host

h3. Secondary (investigate)
* Allocations: +<= 1 allocation per request on hot paths (prefill/decode); +<= 5% increase in allocated bytes/request
* Tail amplification: p99 should not worsen by > 2% without explanation (e.g., known background compaction)
* GPU kernel launch count: no > 1% increase in launches for prefill/decode kernels (excluding telemetry kernels; there should not be any)
* Contention: no new mutex hotspots in telemetry fast-path

h3. Hard stops (rollback triggers)
Any of the following is an automatic rollback / disable-flag recommendation:
* p95 latency regression > 2% sustained for > 15 minutes under steady load
* throughput drop > 2% sustained for > 15 minutes
* evidence of GPU stream synchronization introduced by telemetry (e.g., cudaDeviceSynchronize, event waits on critical path)
* OOM or near-OOM due to telemetry buffers (e.g., ring buffer growth, unbounded tags)
* high cardinality symptoms causing runtime backpressure (telemetry sink blocking)

h2. Test prerequisites
h3. Build and runtime requirements
* Two binaries or images:
** Baseline: telemetry disabled (compile-time or runtime) and verified to produce *zero* cache telemetry events
** Telemetry-enabled: identical commit except telemetry code paths enabled behind flags
* Feature flags (names may vary by runtime train; confirm with runtime config):
** cache_telemetry_v2_enabled
** cache_telemetry_v2_sampling_rate
** cache_telemetry_v2_emit_per_request_events (should be OFF for most perf runs unless explicitly measuring it)

h3. Environment
* Dedicated perf cluster (preferred) or perf-canary environment with isolated tenants
* Fixed GPU clocks when possible (to reduce variance)
* Disable noisy neighbors / batch jobs
* Ensure identical driver/CUDA versions between runs

h3. Models and workloads
Choose at least one representative model and one “worst case” stress workload.
Recommended minimum set:
* Model: Llama-3-class 8B/70B equivalent (use internal model alias used by perf-canary)
* Workloads (run all):
** W1: Short prompts, short outputs (e.g., prompt 256 tok, output 128 tok)
** W2: Long prompt prefill heavy (prompt 4k–8k tok, output 128 tok)
** W3: Long decode heavy (prompt 256 tok, output 2k tok)
** W4: Mixed distribution (prod-like histogram)

Cache regimes to force (if supported by harness):
* R1: ~10% hit-rate (nearly cold)
* R2: ~50% hit-rate
* R3: ~85% hit-rate (highly cacheable / normalized prompts)

Note: If hit-rate cannot be forced, record observed hit-rate and report results as a function of it.

h2. What to measure
Report metrics for each run and compare baseline vs telemetry-enabled:

h3. End-to-end metrics
* Request latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 (ms)
* Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming (ms)
* Throughput: requests/s and tokens/s
* Error rate (must be equal; otherwise results are invalid)

h3. Runtime internals
* Prefill time and decode time breakdown (if available)
* Scheduler queueing time
* Cache path counters (lookup/insert/evict) to ensure code paths were exercised

h3. CPU metrics
* CPU time (user/system), context switches
* Allocation rate (allocs/s, bytes/s)
* Lock contention hotspots

h3. GPU metrics
* SM occupancy / achieved occupancy
* Kernel time distribution for prefill/decode kernels
* H2D/D2H memcopy volume (should not change)
* GPU launch and synchronization stats

h2. Methodology
h3. Overview
For each workload W and cache regime R:
# Run baseline N times
# Run telemetry-enabled N times
# Compare distributions and compute overhead

We recommend:
* N = 5 runs minimum per condition
* Warmup window: 2–5 minutes
* Measurement window: 10–20 minutes steady state
* Fixed concurrency and QPS (avoid closed-loop artifacts unless intentionally testing backpressure)

h3. Controlling variance
* Use the same request corpus and random seed
* Pin the same GPU set (no re-scheduling between runs)
* Reboot node only if required; otherwise keep OS state stable
* Record:
** runtime git SHA
** config file
** driver/CUDA versions
** kernel version
** GPU SKU and clocks

h2. Step-by-step: running the perf harness
This section assumes the standard internal perf runner is available. If you are using perf-canary, follow the same baseline vs enabled split.

h3. 1) Prepare configs
Create two config files differing only in telemetry flags.

*Baseline (telemetry OFF)*
{code}
cache_telemetry_v2_enabled: false
cache_telemetry_v2_sampling_rate: 0
cache_telemetry_v2_emit_per_request_events: false
{code}

*Telemetry-enabled (default sampling)*
{code}
cache_telemetry_v2_enabled: true
cache_telemetry_v2_sampling_rate: 0.05
cache_telemetry_v2_emit_per_request_events: false
{code}

*Telemetry-enabled (worst-case sampling; use only for bounding)*
{code}
cache_telemetry_v2_enabled: true
cache_telemetry_v2_sampling_rate: 1.0
cache_telemetry_v2_emit_per_request_events: true
{code}

Important:
* The “worst-case” configuration is expected to be more expensive and is used only to confirm that overhead scales predictably and to detect pathological blocking.

h3. 2) Run load test (example commands)
Replace placeholders with the actual harness and endpoints used in your environment.

Example (closed-loop concurrency test):
{code}
# Baseline
perf-runner \
  --target http://127.0.0.1:8080 \
  --model redwood/llama3-70b \
  --workload W2_long_prefill.json \
  --concurrency 64 \
  --duration 20m \
  --warmup 3m \
  --config runtime-baseline.yaml \
  --out results/baseline_W2_R2

# Telemetry enabled
perf-runner \
  --target http://127.0.0.1:8080 \
  --model redwood/llama3-70b \
  --workload W2_long_prefill.json \
  --concurrency 64 \
  --duration 20m \
  --warmup 3m \
  --config runtime-telemetry.yaml \
  --out results/telemetry_W2_R2
{code}

Example (open-loop fixed QPS):
{code}
perf-runner \
  --target http://127.0.0.1:8080 \
  --workload W4_mixed.json \
  --qps 120 \
  --duration 20m \
  --warmup 3m \
  --config runtime-telemetry.yaml
{code}

h3. 3) Validate test integrity
Before analyzing overhead, ensure:
* Same request count (within 1–2%)
* Same error rate (0 preferred)
* Similar achieved QPS/concurrency
* Observed cache hit-rate is in the expected band
* No background cluster events (node eviction, GPU reset)

h2. CPU profiling procedures
Run CPU profiling on the telemetry-enabled build first to detect obvious hotspots, then compare to baseline.

h3. Linux perf (sampling)
{code}
# Identify PID
pidof redwood-runtime

# Capture 60s profile
sudo perf record -F 99 -p <PID> -g -- sleep 60
sudo perf report --stdio > perf_report.txt
{code}

What to look for:
* Any new top-of-stack entries in telemetry modules (event formatting, hashing, tag map operations)
* Mutex contention in telemetry sink
* Excessive time in string formatting / JSON serialization (should be avoided on hot path)

h3. Heap/alloc profiling (jemalloc or tcmalloc)
Use the allocator tooling enabled in your build. Example patterns:
{code}
# If jemalloc profiling is enabled
export MALLOC_CONF="prof:true,prof_active:true,lg_prof_interval:28"

# Run test, then dump profile (mechanism depends on runtime integration)
kill -SIGUSR1 <PID>
{code}

Acceptance guidance:
* Telemetry should not introduce per-token allocations.
* Per-request allocations should be bounded and ideally amortized via pooling.

h3. pprof (if enabled)
If runtime exposes pprof endpoints:
{code}
curl -o cpu.pb.gz http://127.0.0.1:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=60
go tool pprof -http=:0 cpu.pb.gz
{code}

h2. GPU profiling procedures
Goal: ensure telemetry does not introduce GPU sync points or alter kernel schedule.

h3. NVIDIA Nsight Systems (nsys)
Capture a short representative window (30–90 seconds) at steady state.
{code}
sudo nsys profile \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=cpu \
  --duration=60 \
  --output=nsys_telemetry_W2 \
  --capture-range=nvtx \
  --capture-range-end=stop \
  --force-overwrite=true \
  --attach-pid=<PID>
{code}

Notes:
* If NVTX ranges are available for prefill/decode, use them to reduce noise.
* Compare baseline and telemetry-enabled timelines for:
** additional CUDA API calls on critical path
** device syncs
** increased CPU launch overhead that shifts GPU idle gaps

h3. NVIDIA Nsight Compute (ncu) (targeted)
Use sparingly; it perturbs performance.
{code}
sudo ncu --set full --target-processes pid --pid <PID> --launch-skip 100 --launch-count 20
{code}

Look for changes in:
* achieved occupancy
* memory throughput
* kernel duration for prefill/decode kernels

h3. DCGM / nvidia-smi monitoring
During each run, record:
{code}
# GPU util and memory at 1s interval
nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1 -o TD > gpu_dmon.txt

# Or DCGM if available
dcgmi dmon -e 100,101,150,155 -d 1000 > dcgm_dmon.txt
{code}

h2. Telemetry-specific overhead traps (common failure modes)
If overhead exceeds thresholds, investigate these first:

h3. Hot-path string work
Symptoms:
* CPU increases disproportionately with QPS
* perf shows time in fmt/printf, string concatenation, JSON encoding

Mitigation:
* Precompute/encode tag keys; use integer IDs or enums
* Avoid per-event string allocation
* Use fixed-size buffers or ring buffers

h3. Lock contention in sink
Symptoms:
* Increased context switches
* perf shows mutex/condvar hotspots

Mitigation:
* Use per-thread buffers with batched flush
* Reduce flush frequency; avoid synchronous writes

h3. Accidental GPU sync
Symptoms:
* nsys shows cudaDeviceSynchronize / event waits during request processing
* GPU idle gaps increase

Mitigation:
* Ensure saved_prefill_ms estimation is CPU-side and does not call blocking CUDA APIs
* Avoid querying GPU timing from request thread

h3. Sampling misconfiguration
Symptoms:
* High overhead only when sampling rate is high
* Excessive event volume

Mitigation:
* Set sane defaults (e.g., 1–5% sampling for per-request events)
* Keep aggregated counters always-on; keep per-request events sampled

h2. Reporting template
Attach this to the Linear issue/PR and post summary in #eng-runtime.

*Test metadata*
* Date:
* Runtime SHA:
* Baseline image/tag:
* Telemetry image/tag:
* Model:
* GPU SKU / count:
* Driver/CUDA:
* Flags (sampling rate, per-request events):

*Workload summary*
| Workload | Cache regime | Observed hit-rate | Notes |

*Results (baseline vs telemetry)*
| Metric | Baseline | Telemetry | Delta |
| p50 latency (ms) |  |  |  |
| p95 latency (ms) |  |  |  |
| p99 latency (ms) |  |  |  |
| TTFT p95 (ms) |  |  |  |
| tokens/s/GPU |  |  |  |
| GPU util avg (%) |  |  |  |
| CPU avg (cores) |  |  |  |

*Conclusion*
* Pass/Fail vs acceptance thresholds:
* Any suspected root causes:
* Recommended next action: ship / ship with lower sampling / fix & rerun

h2. Rollback guidance
If any *Hard stop* trigger occurs in perf-canary or production canary:

Immediate actions:
# Disable flags in the affected environment:
** cache_telemetry_v2_enabled = false (or reduce sampling to 0)
# Confirm latency/throughput recover within 10–15 minutes
# Post in #eng-runtime and #eng-sre with:
** time window
** region/tier
** observed deltas
** graphs/screenshots
# File/upgrade a blocking issue with owner (Runtime: Omar El-Sayed; Perf: Marcus Reed)

h2. Appendix: recommended run matrix (minimum)
Minimum gating set (per GPU SKU in perf cluster):
* W1 @ R1 and R3 (sanity for cold/hot cache)
* W2 @ R2 (prefill-heavy)
* W3 @ R2 (decode-heavy)
* W4 @ observed prod-like hit-rate

If you can only run one workload, choose *W2_long_prefill* because cache telemetry touches prefill-adjacent accounting and tends to surface overhead.

h2. Appendix: interpreting small deltas
If deltas are within +/-0.5% but inconsistent across runs:
* Increase run count to N=10
* Ensure the host is not frequency scaling (CPU governor)
* Check for background disk/network activity
* Verify sampling configuration matches across runs

If deltas are small but monotonic (always worse with telemetry):
* Consider it real; investigate CPU profiles for small but consistent hotspots

h2. Changelog
* 2025-02-10: Initial version for KV/prefix cache telemetry v2 rollout.
* 2025-02-18: Added hard-stop rollback triggers and worst-case sampling guidance.
* 2025-02-24: Updated acceptance thresholds to align with runtime train gating (+<=1% p95).
